text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Demand for workers in small- and medium-sized businesses set to rise by 80,000 jobs this year, accelerating from last year's 71,500. (p1)
- Transport group Nedlloyd and Rotterdam port services group Vigilanter plan to sell their 40 pct stake in tug company Smit Internationale. (p1)
- Manufacturing industry confidence continues to rise in April; companies pleased with order books. (p1)
- Belgium's cooperative bank Bacob is eyeing France's financial service group Cie financiere de Paribas' Dutch unit Banque Paribas Nederland. (p1)
- Royal Dutch/Shell appoints Dutchman Ron van den Berg new managing director of Shell Nigeria. (p3)
- Rabo Securities exercises the green shoe over-allotment option in shares of Computer Services Solutions (CSS), which it launched on the New Market Amsterdam (NMAX). (p3)
- Computer automation company Origin is to reorganise in order to better serve its parent Philips Electronics (p5)
- Civil servants pension fund ABP seeks more flexibility in its property investments. (p13)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Banks, among which U.S. bank J.P Morgan, praise Dutch economic growth. (p1)
- ABN Amro bank, securities bank Kempen & Co and National Investment Bank NIB seek to continue market for unquoted stocks. (p2)
- Temp agency Randstad issues falcons (fixed-term agreements for long-term call options) on some three percent of its shares. (p2)
- Shareholders incensed at Sanderink Beheer's meagre takeover bid for information technology company Multihouse. (p17)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Transhipment of goods through Amsterdam Port grows 12.9 pct in first quarter compared to same period in 1996. (p6)
- Building under ground in the Netherlands has great possiblities in the future, study by Technical University Delft shows. (p9)
- Builder Wilma says not seeking bourse listing now planned merger with rival BAM has fallen through. (p27)
TROUW
- Zwolle-based soap plant De Nieuwe Fenix to close down. (p7)
- Publisher Wolters Kluwer in talks with France's Altedia Communications on taking over some of Altedia's activities. (p16)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Engineering group Holec Machines plans to split up its activities into two or three independent units. (p12)
